title: `strip_comments=True` removes optimizer hints like `/*+ DIRECT */`
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

Optimizer hints are written as comments, but they change the query plan, and `strip_comments` deletes them along with ordinary comments.

```python
import sqlparse
sqlparse.format('insert /*+ DIRECT */ into sch.table_name as select * from foo', strip_comments=True)
```
Expected: the input unchanged.
Actual: `'insert   into sch.table_name as select * from foo'`

Single-line hints are dropped as well: `sqlparse.format('select --+full(u)\n--comment simple', strip_comments=True)` should give `'select --+full(u)\n'` (only the plain comment removed), but gives `'select\n'`.

The rule: `strip_comments` must keep every hint comment (`/*+ ... */`, `--+ ...`, `#+ ...`) exactly as written, and still remove all ordinary comments around them. For example `SELECT /*+cluster(T)*/* FROM T_EEE T where A >:1` is returned unchanged, and an empty string stays empty.
acceptance: Multi-line and single-line hint comments survive `strip_comments=True` unchanged
Ordinary comments next to hints are still removed
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
